title: Vendor Query Redaction & Oncall Evidence Addendum (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This addendum proposes minimum contractual controls for vendors who are granted live access to customer inference requests for operational support (e.g., oncall debugging, live tailing, incident troubleshooting). The goal is to ensure predictable redaction behavior, short-lived evidence capture, and clear auditability that satisfies enterprise customers and our compliance reviewers.

Scope:
- Applies to third-party vendors and integrators that receive real-time or near-real-time visibility into unredacted or partially redacted inference queries/responses.
- Not intended for bulk model training data transfers, which are covered by the DPA and separate training/derivative-works exhibits.

Key definitions (working):
- "Live access": any mechanism enabling a vendor engineer to view, query, or replay inference traffic in less than 1 hour latency (includes live tail, proxy debug sessions, and interactive sessions).
- "Query evidence": logs, screen captures, packet captures, session transcripts, or KV-cache extracts used for troubleshooting an incident or bug report.
- "Redaction": automated or manual removal/obfuscation of PII and sensitive tokens from query evidence prior to storage or vendor access.
- "Ephemeral window": the maximum time query evidence may remain accessible in a recoverable form before deletion (proposed 72 hours).

Minimum contractual controls (proposed language snippets):
1) Permitted Purpose and Strict Scope
   - Vendor may access live inference traffic only for the narrow purpose of troubleshooting and resolving operational incidents, as defined in this addendum. Access for product development, model tuning, or training is expressly prohibited unless separately agreed in writing.

2) Redaction Requirements
   - All query evidence stored or transmitted to Vendor must first pass Redwood's automated redaction pipeline (see Appendix A). The pipeline must remove or mask: names, contact info, government IDs, financial account numbers, full credit card numbers, and any customer-designated sensitive fields.
   - Where automated redaction cannot deterministically identify sensitive elements (e.g., freeform text with potential PII), evidence must be provisioned in a secure ephemeral view only and labeled "review-required". Vendor engineers may only access review-required items after explicit request and approval from the Redwood incident owner.

3) Ephemeral Access & Retention
   - Ephemeral window: query evidence retained in a decryptable form for troubleshooting must be deleted within 72 hours from capture unless an incident classification requires longer retention (max extension: 14 days with documented justification and CSO approval).
   - Immutable audit markers (hashes, metadata) may be retained indefinitely for audit and non-reversible evidence-of-access purposes. These markers must not contain PII or customer content.

4) Access Controls and Authentication
   - Vendor access must use mTLS client certificates bound to a single engineer identity and require MFA. Shared accounts are forbidden.
   - Access tokens or short-lived credentials provisioned for a session must expire within 15 minutes of inactivity and be revocable via an API.

5) Evidence Handling & Proof-of-Deletion
   - Vendor must provide proof-of-deletion within 24 hours of a deletion request from Redwood, in the form of signed deletion receipts and log entries that reference the original evidence ID. Proof format: SHA256(original-evidence-id || deletion-timestamp || vendor-kid) signed by vendor KMS key.
   - Forensic copies retained by Vendor for billing or legal hold must be enumerated and subject to Redwood quarterly spot checks.

6) Monitoring, Audit & Reporting
   - All vendor view/actions (open event, copy, export, session start/stop) must be logged and forwarded to Redwood's telemetry endpoint in near-real-time (max 5 min delay).
   - Redwood reserves the right to request a time-bound evidence trail export (sample set) for independent audit. Vendor will respond within 5 business days.

7) Incident Escalation and Remediation
   - If a confirmed leakage of sensitive customer content occurs due to Vendor misconfiguration or negligence, Vendor must: (a) notify Redwood within 1 hour of detection, (b) provide root cause within 48 hours, and (c) remediate exposures and submit an external attestation within 7 days.

8) Contractual Remedies and Liability
   - Loss related to unauthorized retention or distribution of customer content shall be subject to the liability cap in the base agreement—but for gross negligence or willful misconduct, Redwood may seek equitable remedies and injunctive relief.

Appendix A: Automated Redaction Pipeline (high-level)
- Stage 1: Field-level classifiers (JSON schemas) strip clearly labeled PII fields.
- Stage 2: Named-entity recognition (NER) ensemble with threshold; low-confidence hits flagged "review-required".
- Stage 3: Rule-backed token filters for known sensitive patterns (SSNs, CCs).
- Stage 4: Final output: either "redacted artifact" or "ephemeral review artifact".

Operational playbook notes (working / not final):
- "Review-required" flow: Redwood incident owner creates a short-lived session and sends an 'access ticket' via secure slack channel #sec-oncall (ticket format: SEC-TICKET-<id>).
- Every manual access requires two approvers (incident owner + CSO delegate) during business hours; single approver out-of-hours with explicit justification.
- TODO: define storage encryption envelope (KMS vs vendor-managed HSM). See JIRA SEC-6543 for background.

Negotiation positions (playbook for legal):
- Redwood preferred: 72h ephemeral window, automated redaction mandatory, proof-of-deletion with KMS-signed receipt, quarterly spot checks.
- Vendor likely pushback: longer retention for debugging (7–30 days), resistance to deletion proofs, and objections to per-engineer mTLS requirement.
- Concessions we can accept: allow a 14-day max extension with CSO approval; accept HSM attestation in lieu of KMS-signed receipts if vendor provides quarterly independent audit (SOC2 type II + custom evidence).

Open questions / items for resolution:
- Should we allow customer-specific redaction schemas to be provided by the customer and enforced by vendor? (Pros: more precise redaction; Cons: operational burden and data-sharing risk).
- How do we treat derived diagnostic artifacts (embeddings, aggregated metrics) — classify as non-PII by default? Need product input.
- Evidence-of-deletion format: legal wants cryptographic receipts; infra team prefers API-driven deletion logs. Combine both?

References / links:
- Confluence: "Vendor Oncall Playbook v2" (CONFLUENCE-SEC-1287)
- Jira: SEC-6543 (ephemeral retention proof-of-concept)
- Draft PR for redaction pipeline: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/412

Negotiation checklist (for commercial/legal lead):
- [ ] Insert addendum clause into MSSA as Exhibit X
- [ ] Confirm CSO-approved extension process 
- [ ] Map redaction pipeline owners (Infra, Applied ML, Legal)
- [ ] Create customer-facing FAQ (short blurbs explaining oncall evidence controls)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep language non-technical in the contract; move technical pipeline details to a tech annex (Appendix A can be attached as a non-binding schedule).
- For enterprise customers that require full proof-of-deletion, create a 1-pager explaining proof format + verification steps.
- Slack thread where this started: #sec-vendor-ops (search "redaction addendum")

Next steps (short):
